The summary report is generated based on the following five technical analysis methods: Moving Averages, MACD (Moving Average Convergence Divergence), Fibonacci Retracement, Bollinger Bands & Relative Strength Index (RSI).

Moving Averages (MA) is a trend-following indicator that helps smooth out price data by creating a постоянно moving average of a specified number of periods. The MA can be used to identify the overall trend of a security and to determine whether it is in an uptrend or a downtrend. 

The Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD) is a trend-following momentum indicator that shows the relationship between two moving averages of a security's price. The MACD can be used to identify changes in the momentum of a security and to determine whether it is overbought or oversold.

The Fibonacci Retracement is a technical analysis tool that is used to identify potential support and resistance levels. The Fibonacci Retracement levels are based on the Fibonacci sequence, which is a series of numbers in which each number is the sum of the two preceding ones. The Fibonacci Retracement levels are used to identify areas where a security may pause or reverse its trend.

Bollinger Bands are a volatility indicator that helps identify whether a security is overbought or oversold. The Bollinger Bands are created by calculating the moving average of a security's price and then adding and subtracting two standard deviations. The Bollinger Bands can be used to identify potential trading opportunities and to determine the volatility of a security.

The Relative Strength Index (RSI) is a momentum indicator that measures the magnitude of recent price changes to evaluate overbought or oversold conditions in the price of a stock. RSI is a measure of the speed and change of price movements. It is a momentum oscillator that measures the magnitude of recent price changes to evaluate overbought or oversold conditions in the price of a stock.
